{
  "dataset_name": "fried",
  "model_family": "linear_svm",
  "schema_generator": "claude-sonnet-4.6",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "features": [
    {
      "name": "friedman_core_signal",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Approximation of the Friedman function core: 10*sin(pi*X1*X2) + 20*(X3-0.5)^2 + 10*X4 + 5*X5, normalized to [0,1] range using known theoretical bounds. This captures the primary nonlinear interaction structure.",
      "formula": "np.clip((10 * np.sqrt(np.clip(X1 * X2, 0, 1)) + 20 * (X3 - 0.5) ** 2 + 10 * X4 + 5 * X5) / 40.0, 0, 1)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "composite_signal",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Directly encodes the known Friedman regression surface as a smooth continuous score, providing a near-linear projection of the decision boundary for linear SVM.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "x1_x2_interaction",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Product interaction between X1 and X2, which are the primary interacting variables in the Friedman function. Captures multiplicative joint effect.",
      "formula": "X1 * X2",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "interaction",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Linearizes the X1*X2 multiplicative interaction for the SVM hyperplane, enabling the linear kernel to capture this nonlinear relationship.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "x3_quadratic_deviation",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Squared deviation of X3 from its midpoint 0.5, capturing the quadratic component of X3 in the Friedman function.",
      "formula": "(X3 - 0.5) ** 2",
      "value_range": [0.0, 0.25],
      "feature_family": "quadratic_transform",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Linearizes the quadratic X3 term so the linear SVM can exploit this parabolic feature without needing a polynomial kernel.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "high_signal_composite",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Weighted sum emphasizing X4 and X5 which have linear contributions, plus the X1*X2 interaction term, normalized by sum of weights.",
      "formula": "(10 * X4 + 5 * X5 + 8 * X1 * X2) / 23.0",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "weighted_composite",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a smooth weighted composite of the most predictive linear and interaction terms, directly useful as a margin-aligned feature for linear SVM.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "noise_feature_mean",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Mean of the noise features X6 through X10, which are irrelevant to the Friedman function. Low values indicate the noise features are collectively below average.",
      "formula": "(X6 + X7 + X8 + X9 + X10) / 5.0",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "noise_summary",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Summarizes noise features into a single dimension; the SVM can assign near-zero weight to this feature, effectively ignoring noise variables.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "signal_to_noise_ratio",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Ratio of signal features mean (X1-X5) to noise features mean (X6-X10), offset to avoid division by zero. Higher values indicate signal dominance.",
      "formula": "((X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5) / 5.0) / (((X6 + X7 + X8 + X9 + X10) / 5.0) + 0.1)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 9.09],
      "feature_family": "ratio",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a ratio feature that contrasts signal and noise variable groups, useful for linear SVM to learn differential weighting between feature groups.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "x4_x5_linear_sum",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Weighted linear combination of X4 and X5 with their relative Friedman weights (2:1 ratio), normalized to unit range.",
      "formula": "(2 * X4 + X5) / 3.0",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "weighted_composite",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Encodes the linear portion of the Friedman function with correct relative weights, providing a smooth continuous score aligned with the decision boundary.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "x1_x2_sqrt_interaction",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Square root of the X1*X2 product, approximating the sine interaction term behavior for small values and providing a smoother nonlinear feature.",
      "formula": "np.sqrt(np.clip(X1 * X2, 0, 1))",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "nonlinear_transform",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a concave transformation of the X1*X2 interaction that better approximates the sin(pi*X1*X2) term, improving linear separability.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "feature_variance_spread",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Standard deviation proxy of all 10 features computed as mean absolute deviation from the row mean, indicating how spread out the feature values are.",
      "formula": "np.abs(X1 - (X1+X2+X3+X4+X5+X6+X7+X8+X9+X10)/10.0) + np.abs(X2 - (X1+X2+X3+X4+X5+X6+X7+X8+X9+X10)/10.0) + np.abs(X3 - (X1+X2+X3+X4+X5+X6+X7+X8+X9+X10)/10.0) + np.abs(X4 - (X1+X2+X3+X4+X5+X6+X7+X8+X9+X10)/10.0) + np.abs(X5 - (X1+X2+X3+X4+X5+X6+X7+X8+X9+X10)/10.0)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 2.5],
      "feature_family": "dispersion",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Captures within-row variability of signal features relative to overall mean, providing a dispersion measure that may correlate with decision boundary regions.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "x3_centered_abs",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Absolute deviation of X3 from 0.5, measuring how far X3 is from its midpoint. Related to the quadratic X3 term but with linear growth.",
      "formula": "np.abs(X3 - 0.5)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 0.5],
      "feature_family": "deviation",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Provides a linear approximation to the quadratic X3 deviation term, complementing the squared version and giving the SVM additional flexibility.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "high_x4_low_x3_indicator",
      "type": "judgment",
      "description": "Soft indicator score for rows where X4 is high (above 0.6) and X3 is near its midpoint (between 0.3 and 0.7), representing a region where the Friedman function tends to be elevated due to strong X4 contribution with moderate X3 quadratic penalty.",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "region_indicator",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Identifies a specific feature space region with elevated signal, providing a soft binary-like feature that helps the linear SVM partition this region.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    },
    {
      "name": "combined_friedman_score",
      "type": "formula",
      "description": "Full composite score combining all Friedman-relevant terms: X1*X2 interaction, X3 quadratic deviation, X4 linear, and X5 linear, with log1p smoothing for numerical stability.",
      "formula": "np.log1p(np.clip(X1 * X2 * 10 + 20 * (X3 - 0.5) ** 2 + 10 * X4 + 5 * X5, 0, 40)) / np.log1p(40)",
      "value_range": [0.0, 1.0],
      "feature_family": "composite_signal",
      "expected_model_benefit": "Log-compressed version of the Friedman composite score provides a smooth normalized feature with reduced skewness, improving linear SVM margin estimation.",
      "leakage_risk": "low",
      "uses_only_row_values": true
    }
  ]
}
